title: Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan

cards.h: Three neighbours, three kinds of problem
cards.b:
Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan all share long open borders with India. Each tests a different side of Indian policy: Bangladesh (water, migration, politics), Nepal (a special treaty, a boundary dispute, China) and Bhutan (a close security partner with a China question).

From 2024 to 2026 politics changed in all three. Sheikh Hasina fell in Bangladesh (August 2024), Nepal's government was toppled by youth protests (September 2025), and both held elections in early 2026.

The exam wants three things: the treaty framework, the irritants and the current shifts. Write "as of 2026" for anything recent.

The Land Boundary Agreement (1974, ratified in 2015) exchanged 111 Indian enclaves for 51 Bangladeshi ones. The Constitution (100th Amendment) Act, 2015 gave effect to it. India has also given large lines of credit and built rail and road links, and bought power from Bangladesh.

Bangladesh is India's largest trading partner in South Asia (about $13 billion in 2023-24, mostly Indian exports). India offers duty-free access to most goods.

• Teesta: a sharing deal was nearly ready in 2011 but West Bengal objected. China has offered to fund a Teesta project.
  • Ganga Water Treaty (12 December 1996) runs for 30 years, so it expires in December 2026. As of late 2026 renewal talks were reported to be at an early stage, and a parliamentary committee in India warned of delay.
  • Border killings, migration and 'push-ins' along the 4,096 km border.
  • Trade barriers: non-tariff barriers, and India's 2025 curbs on some Bangladeshi imports and the withdrawal of a transshipment facility after tough remarks from Dhaka's interim government.
  • Minorities: attacks on Hindus drew Indian concern in 2024–25.
  • Hasina in India: she has lived in India since 5 August 2024. A Bangladeshi tribunal sentenced her to death in absentia in November 2025. Dhaka wants her extradited. India has not agreed.

The interim government under Muhammad Yunus ruled from August 2024. The Awami League was barred from the 12 February 2026 election, which the BNP won with a two-thirds majority (about 209 of 297 declared seats). Tarique Rahman became prime minister on 17 February 2026.

India sent Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri to the swearing-in. Modi invited Rahman to India. Analysts expect a reset but a more 'balanced' Bangladesh that deals with China and Pakistan too.

India's agenda: border security, minority rights, extradition questions, transit and connectivity (Akhaura–Agartala rail, Chattogram port access), energy, and a Ganga treaty renewal.

Bangladesh's agenda: Teesta, border killings, trade access, a new Ganga deal and a fair visa regime.

The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship allows an open border and free movement of people. Its Article 7 gives Indians and Nepalis reciprocal rights to reside, work and own property. Gorkha regiments in the Indian Army come from Nepal.

India is Nepal's biggest trade partner and transit route, since Nepal is landlocked. Hydropower, rail (Jaynagar–Kurtha) and pipelines (Motihari–Amlekhgunj, South Asia's first cross-border petroleum pipeline, 2019) deepen ties.

Irritants:

  • The 2015 blockade after Nepal's new Constitution, which Madhesis felt left them out.
  • Kalapani–Lipulekh–Limpiyadhura: in 2020 Nepal published a new map and amended its Constitution to include them.
  • Nepal calls for revision of the 1950 treaty (the Eminent Persons Group report, 2018, was never formally received).
  • The Agnipath scheme (2022) stalled Gorkha recruitment.

cards.h: Nepal after the Gen Z protests
cards.b:
In September 2025, a ban on social media and anger at corruption set off youth protests. Parliament buildings were burned. PM K.P. Sharma Oli resigned, and former Chief Justice Sushila Karki led an interim government.

In the election on 5 March 2026, the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) under former Kathmandu mayor Balendra (Balen) Shah won almost two-thirds of the seats. Shah, aged 35, became Nepal's youngest prime minister on 27 March 2026.

Early signs are mixed. Modi congratulated him, but reports describe friction over diplomatic protocol, and a wariness about both India and China. Shah has dropped a Chinese-funded industrial park near the Siliguri Corridor from his plans. China's Belt and Road framework (signed December 2024 under Oli) remains a factor.

India's aim: stable ties and early delivery on hydropower, rail and trade.

The 1949 Treaty of Friendship was revised in 2007 to remove the clause requiring Bhutan to be 'guided' by India in foreign policy. Now it asks for close consultation on national security interests.

  • Hydropower: India helps build and buys power: Chukha, Tala, Mangdechhu (720 MW, 2019) and Punatsangchhu. It is Bhutan's largest source of revenue.
  • Doklam (2017): India acted to protect Bhutan's claim and its own Siliguri Corridor. China and Bhutan hold boundary talks; India watches any deal on Doklam.
  • Gelephu Mindfulness City: a large special region announced by Bhutan's king in December 2023. India has agreed on rail links to Gelephu and Samtse (approved in 2025) and Modi visited Bhutan in November 2025.
  • Bhutan was the first country to receive Indian vaccines in 2021.

India's neighbours complain of asymmetry: India sets the pace. They also use China as leverage, which scholars call hedging. India's reply, in the 'Neighbourhood First' policy, is to provide public goods quickly and not to interfere in internal politics.

The common thread in 2024–26: when India is seen as backing a single ruling group (Hasina in Bangladesh, parties in Nepal), a change of government leads to a backlash. India now stresses people-to-people ties and engages all parties.

cards.h: India's playbook, and its test in 2026
cards.b:
• Connectivity: Integrated Check Posts, Bangladesh rail links, Nepal's rail and pipeline, Bhutan's rail plan.
  • Energy grid: India transmits Nepali and Bhutanese hydropower to Bangladesh through its grid, a rare tri-lateral success (2024).
  • Money and aid: lines of credit, grants and rupee trade.
  • Security: border management, intelligence sharing, defence training for Bhutan and Nepal.
  • Crisis help: the 2015 Nepal earthquake, Covid vaccines, fuel and fertiliser support.

The 2026 test is to reset with new governments in Dhaka and Kathmandu without taking sides, to renew the Ganga treaty in time, and to avoid being seen as shielding Hasina. India's quick outreach to Tarique Rahman and Balen Shah shows this approach.

"Evaluate India's relations with Bangladesh after August 2024." (typical)
"The India-Nepal relationship is described as 'roti-beti'. Examine its challenges." (typical)
"Discuss India-Bhutan ties in the context of China's presence." (typical)

Structure for each country: (1) treaty base; (2) cooperation areas; (3) irritants; (4) China's role; (5) 2024–26 developments; (6) way forward.

Use a comparison table across the three. Keep the Ganga treaty expiry (December 2026) and Kalapani as your key hooks.

quiz.q: The Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh was signed in:
The 2015 Land Boundary Agreement was given effect by which Constitution Amendment?
Tarique Rahman became Bangladesh's Prime Minister in:
quiz.w: Sworn in on 17 February 2026 after the BNP won the 12 February election.

quiz.q: The India–Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship was signed in:
Which three places are at the heart of the India–Nepal boundary dispute?
quiz.w: Nepal claims Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura; its 2020 map included them.

quiz.q: Nepal's youngest Prime Minister, elected in 2026, is:
quiz.w: Balendra Shah of the RSP, aged 35, took office on 27 March 2026.

quiz.q: The revised India–Bhutan Friendship Treaty dates from:
quiz.w: The 2007 version dropped the clause on being 'guided' by India.

quiz.q: Doklam, the site of the 2017 standoff, lies near:
o: The Siliguri Corridor and the Bhutan-China-India tri-junction
quiz.w: It lies at the tri-junction, close to the Siliguri Corridor.

quiz.q: Which river-sharing issue is a major irritant with Bangladesh and stalled over West Bengal's objection?
quiz.w: The Teesta sharing deal was blocked in 2011.

quiz.q: The Motihari–Amlekhgunj pipeline was notable as:
o: India's first gas pipeline to Pakistan
South Asia's first cross-border petroleum pipeline
quiz.w: It was commissioned in 2019 between India and Nepal.
